questions.q: How did Alan react when David spoke well of his friend Mr. Campbell the minister?
choices: He said he hated everyone with that name
He asked David to tell him more about the man
He laughed and said all ministers were alike
He said the minister must be a distant cousin
questions.evidence: he hated all that were of that name

questions.q: What did Duncan Stewart and the other swordsmen do with the three guineas King George gave each of them?
choices: Spent them on a feast in a London tavern
Handed them to the porter at the palace lodge
Sent them home to their families in the Highlands
Gave them to the soldiers of the Black Watch
questions.evidence: So he gives the King's three guineas into the man's hand

questions.q: Why did Alan's father give his money to the palace porter?
choices: He was afraid the King would take it back
He owed the porter money from an earlier visit
To show the porter what fine gentlemen they were
He thought the King's money would bring them bad luck
questions.evidence: give the poor porter a proper notion of their quality

questions.q: According to Alan, why did he first enlist as a soldier?
choices: His chief ordered him to learn the English way of war
He wanted to see London as his father had
His father left him almost nothing to live on
He was forced into the army by a press gang
questions.evidence: He left me my breeks to cover me, and little besides

questions.q: What did Alan do at the battle of Preston Pans?
choices: Deserted the English army to join the other side
Was badly wounded and carried off the field by his friends
Saved the life of his chief, Ardshiel
Was taken prisoner by the red-coats
questions.evidence: I deserted to the right side at Preston Pans

questions.q: What does Alan carry in his pocket that he hopes will give him some protection?
choices: A letter of pardon signed by King George
A pass from the Campbell factor of Appin
A commission from the King of France
A certificate from the captain of the brig
questions.evidence: I have the King of France's commission in my pocket

questions.q: Alan says, "I weary for my friends and country." What does "weary for" mean here?
choices: Grow tired and bored of
Feel worried and afraid for
Miss and long for
Feel ashamed of
questions.evidence: I weary for my friends and country

questions.q: What is the money in Alan's belt?
choices: Pay he earned as a soldier for the French King
A second rent the Appin tenants gathered for Ardshiel
The captain's payment for taking him to Linnhe Loch
Gold he won from the officers of the brig at cards
questions.evidence: scrape up a second rent for Ardshiel

questions.q: Why does Alan mention seeing Ardshiel buying butter in a French market?
choices: To show how cheap food is in France
To show that his chief has learned to cook
To show how low his great chief has been brought
To show that his chief is hiding there in disguise from spies

questions.q: Who is James of the Glens?
choices: Ardshiel's half-brother, who collects the money
A Campbell lawyer working for the King's factor
The captain of the clan who lives in France
A Highland piper who taught Alan his tunes

questions.q: What did David, though he was a Whig, say about the tenants paying two rents?
choices: He called it foolish
He called it noble
He called it unlawful
He called it a trick

questions.q: Who is the man Alan calls the Red Fox?
choices: Captain Hoseason of the brig Covenant
Red-headed Colin Campbell of Glenure
The Duke of Cumberland, called the Butcher
A red-coat officer who hunted Ardshiel

questions.q: When the Red Fox learned that the tenants were sending a second rent to Ardshiel, what did he do first?
choices: He had James of the Glens arrested
He declared all the farms to let
He raised the rent on every farm
He wrote to the King of France
questions.evidence: He declares all the farms to let

questions.q: Why did the Red Fox's first plan to get new tenants fail?
choices: The Stewart tenants offered a better price than any Campbell
No Campbell was willing to travel so far into Appin
James of the Glens tore up all the papers
King George ordered him to leave the farms alone
questions.evidence: offered him a better price than any Campbell in all broad Scotland

questions.q: Why does David say that killing Colin Campbell would do no good?
choices: The Campbells would burn every house in Appin
Colin was already planning to leave the country
The tenants would lose their farms all the same that year
The Government would just send another factor
questions.evidence: There would be another factor in his shoes

questions.q: How does Alan explain that he can travel the Highlands without being arrested?
choices: He always wears a red-coat uniform as a disguise
If a sentry is in one place, he goes by another
He pays the soldiers with money from his belt
He travels only by boat along the coast at night
questions.evidence: if there's a sentry at one place, ye just go by another

questions.q: What does David say was Alan's worst fault?
choices: A habit of drinking too much of the captain's wine
A childish habit of taking offence and picking quarrels
Spending every penny he had on fine clothes and buttons
A tendency to tell long stories that were not true
questions.evidence: his childish propensity to take offence and to pick quarrels

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: The crew of the brig planning a new attack on Alan and David
Alan telling his story and his hatred of the Red Fox
David and Alan sailing safely through the reefs of Mull
David teaching Alan to read the books he carried
questions.evidence: I have seen many a grim face, but never a grimmer than Alan's when he had named the Red Fox
